app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

rca_tasks.investigation_goal: Epicenter check (failure domain: app/latency). Test the hypothesis that image-provider is the primary source of the ~10s end-to-end latency by confirming image-provider spans contain a single ~10s internal processing span (vs. time spent in proxy). If confirmed, capture any internal call-stack or repeated external calls inside those spans.

Connection check (frontend-proxy <-> image-provider). Proxy behavior check (failure domain: latency/config). Test the hypothesis that frontend-proxy is queuing or exhausting upstream connections to image-provider (connection pool exhaustion, long active requests, or long retry/backoff), by looking at proxy latency/connection metrics and proxy logs for upstream wait/retry messages.

Image-provider pod capacity check (failure domain: app/resource). Test the hypothesis that image-provider is under-provisioned (single replica or resource saturation like CPU/Goroutine/threads causing queuing) by verifying number of pods, their restart/ready state and current CPU/memory and per-pod request concurrency.

Upstream trace-detail check (failure domain: dependency/app). Test the hypothesis that image-provider is performing a blocking external call (e.g., object store or CDN) for each request that is responsible for the ~10s delay by inspecting individual slow traces/end-to-end spans to find child calls from image-provider to any external host and their durations.

Connection check (frontend -> frontend-proxy). Test the hypothesis that frontend service is calling frontend-proxy with configurations (host/port/path/headers/timeouts) that mismatch the proxy's accepted listener or are triggering proxy behavior (large requests/streaming) that amplifies latency. Verify frontend's configured upstream and confirm frontend-proxy listener/service matches.

This indicates the proxy (frontend-proxy/Envoy) is where the ~10s is spent (likely waiting on upstream/connection behavior) rather than inside image-provider.

final_report.root_cause: The frontend-proxy (Envoy) is the immediate source of the ~10s request latency: multiple high-latency traces show the ~10,000 ms duration recorded on Envoy/frontend-proxy server spans (operation GET) with response_flags="DI", while the image-provider router egress and image-provider server spans are very short (≈0–675 ms). Exact root mechanism (e.g., specific Envoy cluster/timeout config, downstream client behavior, or an intermittent network/proxy event) could not be proven because Envoy cluster/timeouts and Envoy upstream metrics were not available from the collected data.

In representative traces the long duration is on Envoy frontend-proxy server spans (~10,000 ms) with response_flags="DI"; the image-provider server spans are near-zero duration and the router egress (proxy->upstream) spans are short (~349–675 µs/ms). 2) Service config: kubectl describe confirms image-provider Service/port/endpoints match (ClusterIP, port 8081, endpoint 10.244.1.25:8081) — so no Service name/port/endpoint mismatch. 3) Logs & metrics: frontend-proxy logs show an Envoy warning about no configured global_downstream_max_connections but no upstream connection/timeouts or connection-pool-exhaustion log lines in the inspected window. Prometheus scrapes returned container-level metrics only; Envoy upstream/cluster metrics were not present, preventing metric-level confirmation of connection-pool pressure. 4) Pod capacity: image-provider has a single replica (image-provider-79dbdd7cf4-gnmjv) but pod-level CPU/memory metrics show no saturation (low CPU, ~12% memory usage), so per-pod resource exhaustion is not the cause.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority-weighted investigation conclusions: Priority #1 (Epicenter check): Traces show the ~10s delay is recorded on Envoy/frontend-proxy server spans (response_flags="DI"); image-provider spans are short — therefore the proxy is the latency epicenter, not image-provider internal processing. Priority #2 (Connection check): Kubernetes Service for image-provider is correctly configured and endpoints present, ruling out Service/port/endpoint mismatch. Priority #3 (Proxy behavior): No Envoy upstream metrics available from Prometheus; logs inspected contained an Envoy config warning but no upstream error signs — metric exposure gap blocks deeper confirmation of connection-pool or retry exhaustion. Priority #4 (Capacity): image-provider runs a single replica (operational capacity risk) but is not CPU/memory-saturated, so under-provisioning is a contributing factor (reduces redundancy) but not the proximate cause of the observed 10s latency. Priority #5 (Upstream trace detail): No evidence that image-provider made a blocking external outbound call causing the delay; traces point to proxy/downstream behavior. Overall: evidence consistently localizes the latency to the frontend-proxy/Envoy layer; image-provider is healthy but under-replicated.
